selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main lesson is this passage trying to teach about prayer and major sins?
questions.answer: It teaches that praying is a true human duty, and staying away from major sins fits the way people were created.

questions.question: What teaching method is used to explain this idea?
questions.answer: A comparison using two soldiers.

questions.question: What was special about the first soldier’s training?
questions.answer: He had already been prepared well and took his responsibilities seriously.

questions.question: What was the first soldier like in both skill and character?
questions.answer: He was skilled and careful about doing what was right.

questions.question: Why was he calm about those needs?
questions.answer: He trusted that those needs would be taken care of by the state.

questions.question: What did the good soldier understand about who provides daily needs?
questions.answer: He understood that the state provides those needs.

questions.question: What did the careful soldier believe was his own real job?
questions.answer: His real job was training and fighting.

questions.question: When he did those camp jobs, how did he describe them?
questions.answer: He described them as service he was doing for the state.

questions.question: How did he answer when asked what he was doing?
questions.answer: He said he was carrying out service duties.

questions.question: What false idea did he avoid?
questions.answer: He avoided thinking that his whole purpose was just to earn his food.

questions.question: What does the passage say is suitable for a human being to do?
questions.answer: To perform the prayers and avoid serious sins.

questions.question: Why does the passage use a soldier example?
questions.answer: It helps readers understand the lesson through a clear everyday picture.

questions.question: In the story, what was happening in the country at that time?
questions.answer: There was a broad military call-up.

questions.question: What was he not deeply anxious about?
questions.answer: He was not deeply anxious about his food and supplies.

questions.question: What makes the second soldier a bad example?
questions.answer: He lacks training and thinks mostly about himself.

questions.question: What kinds of help did he expect from the state if needed?
questions.answer: He expected food, equipment, medical care, and even direct help if he became too weak.

questions.question: Besides training and fighting, what other tasks did the disciplined soldier do?
questions.answer: He helped with practical camp jobs like preparing and cleaning eating things.

questions.question: Give two examples of those ordinary tasks.
questions.answer: He prepared cooking items and cleaned eating containers.

questions.question: How did he think about those useful service jobs?
questions.answer: He saw them as assigned duties, not as a personal chase for survival.

questions.question: What can we infer about the attitude of the careful soldier?
questions.answer: He was responsible, trusting, and clear about the difference between his duty and his provision.

questions.question: According to the passage, what two actions match true human duty?
questions.answer: Doing the prescribed prayers and not falling into major sins.

questions.question: What kind of sins are mentioned as things to avoid?
questions.answer: Serious sins.

questions.question: Did he ignore all ordinary tasks related to meals and gear?
questions.answer: No. He still took care of some of them as part of his work.

questions.question: Did his trust make him lazy? Explain.
questions.answer: No. He still did useful service jobs when needed.
